thread:
customer_jess: Hey team — got a customer report: streaming /v1/chat SSE connection drops after ~12s of silence, they get a partial chunk and then a 401 on reconnect. Happening behind ALB + Cloudflare. Repros reliably in our staging with a long-pause response.
support_erin: sorry to hear that — can you paste repro steps + request headers? do they use token rotation?
customer_jess: steps: 1) open SSE to /v1/chat with Bearer token 2) let server stream first chunk then pause for ~15s (we simulate long-latency backend) 3) client sees final chunk truncated then reconnect => 401. curl to reproduce below. No token rotation on client.
customer_jess: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?session=abc"
```
eng_oncall_dan: copy — can you include ALB/CF configuration? have you seen any 502/504 in logs? also need origin vs edge TLS session reuse.
customer_jess: ALB idle timeout 60s, CF proxy with HTTP/2 to origin. No 5xx in our app logs. We do see client-side xhr status 401 on reconnect.
sre_marta: quick note — Cloudflare will pool h2 connections to origin. h2 WINDOW_UPDATE or stream half-close behavior can cause late DATA frames to be buffered then dropped if the edge thinks stream is idle. Could be ALB/LB sending FIN earlier while cf holds connection.
eng_oncall_dan: also common: auth middleware returns 401 for second request because ephemeral token header missing on retry (client didn't resend cookie?) but you said no token rotation. Is the reconnect re-using the same Authorization header?
customer_jess: yes same header. We logged incoming headers on reconnect and Authorization present.
support_erin: can you paste server access log around the event and any nginx/envoy/ALB logs?
customer_jess: pasted sample server access log: 
```
[2026-03-15T17:21:12Z] "GET /v1/chat/stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1" 200 - chunked
[2026-03-15T17:21:25Z] partial payload sent, stream stalled
[2026-03-15T17:21:38Z] new GET /v1/chat/stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1" 401 - reconnect
```
eng_oncall_dan: thanks. can you enable edge proxy trace? app logs show no token error, so likely proxy is resetting the TCP connection after idle and client reconnect hits a different backend or the ALB removed sticky session — 401 could be from our auth layer rejecting ephemeral session id.
sre_marta: share ALB access log snippet too. ALB sometimes sends TCP FIN to connection pool when it sees upstream idle; CF's pooled connection then returns a RST causing truncated data to reach client. Also check if ALB uses http2-to-backend or http1.1; translation can trigger early half-close.
customer_jess: ALB logs: 
```
2026-03-15T17:21:25.123Z elb my-alb 10.0.0.5:12345 10.0.1.9:8080 0.012 0.000 200 200 "GET /v1/chat/stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1"
2026-03-15T17:21:38.999Z elb my-alb 10.0.0.5:12346 10.0.1.9:8080 0.000 0.000 401 401 "GET /v1/chat/stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1"
```
dev-mike: can you try reproducing with direct origin (bypass CF) and with keepalive disabled at ALB? need to isolate CF pooling vs ALB idle close.
support_erin: customer tried bypass -> still saw truncated chunk but reconnect stayed 200. interesting. so CF might be converting/truncating chunk frames only when proxying.
eng_oncall_dan: okay next steps: (1) capture tcpdump on origin while reproducing to confirm whether origin sent final bytes before connection closed; (2) enable Cloudflare origin debug logs (ray id) and compare sequence numbers; (3) try toggling ALB keepalive timeout > client idle; (4) deploy a small sentinel that emits heartbeat every 8s to avoid idle.
sre_marta: also watch for h2 flow control WINDOW_UPDATE exhaustion. If origin stalls and CF sends WINDOW_UPDATE but origin doesn't ack, CF may treat stream as stalled and tear it down — that yields truncated chunk to client.
customer_jess: we captured tcpdump — origin DID send the last chunk: 
```
17:21:24.987 IP 10.0.1.9.8080 > 10.0.0.5.12345: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12390, ack 54321, win 64240, length 45
"data: {\"choices\": [\"partial\"]}\n"
```
then a RST from CF-proxy side a few ms later.
eng_oncall_dan: that points to proxy pooling/halfclose race. For immediate workaround enable application-level keepalive or send SSE comment heartbeats `: heartbeat\n\n` every 10s; longer-term we should recommend setting ALB idle timeout higher than expected pause and disable HTTP/2 pooling on CF if possible.
dev-mike: filed a ticket with CF support to check HTTP/2 stream lifecycle and half-close handling (ticket CF-122334). Deploy-bot: deployed a short-lived keepalive feature to staging for customer.
deploy-bot: rollout started: canary to 3 hosts in staging (runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sse-heartbeat).
support_erin: sent interim workaround to customer (heartbeat and ALB increase). customer will test today and report. :thumbsup:
customer_jess: thanks — will test and update. one last ask: any way to detect on our side when proxy truncated the chunk vs our app failed? what log signature should we search for?
sre_marta: look for TCP RST coming from proxy IP in tcpdump and for mismatch between bytes written by app (application logs) and bytes received by proxy (proxy access logs). our runtime also logs when write syscall returns EPIPE or gets SIGPIPE. filter for those.
eng_oncall_dan: +1. I'll add a brief KB note in support docs about SSE proxy truncation patterns and suggested mitigations.
customer_jess: great, thanks everyone.
